title: Auditor Capture x Information Asymmetry: A Toy Model of Why Third-Party Audits Drift Toward Pass

original_idea.body:
# Auditor Capture x Information Asymmetry: A Toy Model of Why Third-Party Audits Drift Toward Pass

**Problem:** Auditors depend on labs for access/fees; severe information asymmetry. Together they cause systematic optimism.

**Direction:** Construct a principal-agent/repeated-game simulation; identify rubber-stamp conditions; sweep interventions.

**Why it matters:** Mechanism-design lens on why audit mandates fail. No data or lab access.

**Relevant context:** ccgnludelhi.wordpress.com; arXiv:2505.11577; interface-eu.org.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (audit reliability matters for governance) but abstract toy model and indirect catastrophic link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Principal-agent/repeated-game modeling needs solid game-theory fundamentals; intermediate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused modeling deliverable with falsifiable predictions and intervention sweep.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure modeling, fully outside-lab, supports auditable-verification problem.

novelty.reasoning: Auditor capture is a well-developed economics/mechanism-design literature.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Auditor-capture and information-asymmetry models are well-established in economics.
